lucas: quick flag 1h - onboarding magnet-30b-v2 (int4) with a stitched prefill run. After ~19.5k tokens we see a phase ramp -> token-shift: nouns replaced by anchors and occasional repeated 'and and'. float16 and int8 look fine.

maya: can you share a tiny repro and the KVCACHE debug trace? sound like rotary phase misalignment or kv-index wrap.

lucas: minimal repro attached (pasted below). run with `--mode prefill_stream --stitch=true --prefill_stride=2048`
```
./bin/serve --model magnet-30b-v2 --quant=int4 --max-tokens=20000 \
  --prefill_mode=stream --prefill_stride=2048 --kv_index_type=relative
```

alon: relative indexing + compiler-normalized rotary can accumulate phase error. did the model metadata say rotary_base=65536? our compiler uses 10000 by default.

ashley: can you dump `rotary_meta.json` from the model dir and paste `KVCACHE_DEBUG` around token 19000? also try `--rotary_base_override=65536` and `--rotary_scale=1.0` to test.

lucas: pasted snippet from KVCACHE_DEBUG around failure:
```
[19012] kv_index: 18999 rel->abs: 18999
[19012] rotary_phase: 0.9876543 -> 0.0001234 (wrap)
[19013] decoder_token: "and" -> "and" -> repeat
```

prateek: that phase wrap log looks suspicious. if the compiler normalized base, phase values will be scaled; over thousands of positions small mismatch becomes catastrophic. try `--rotary_base_override=10000` (compiler default) and a no-stitch run to separate prefill vs in-flight mismatch.

lucas: kicked off two runs: (A) `prefill_stride=512 + kv_index_type=absolute + rotary_base_override=65536` (B) no-stitch `--stitch=false` + rotary_base_override=65536. queuing artifacts to ci.

ci-bot: nightly_pipeline/run/1789456124 - magnet-30b-v2 longprefill-int4-bisect queued. logs will be at s3://redwood-ci/runs/1789456124/

maya: if (A) fixes it, that points at index conversion bug when relative indices cross stride boundaries. if (B) fixes it, it's stitch-time phase interpolation. both plausible.

alon: also verify quant params: `per_layer_scale` vs `global_scale`. int4 per-layer asymmetric rounding can nudge phase. run with `--quant_fallback=int8` to see if it's purely bitwidth.

lucas: early results: (A) reduced repeats, still occasional anchor tokens at 19.8k. (B) no repeats, stable to 20k. looks like stitch interpolation problem.

ashley: great. next steps: 1) add boundary test that asserts rotary_phase continuity across stitch points; 2) add a test that converts relative->absolute indices against our serialization to catch off-by-one when stride != 1024; 3) run int4 vs int8 parity on the stitch codepath.

prateek: i'll prep a quick bisect PR that toggles `stitch_phase_interpolate` and adds a unit that replays KVCACHE_DEBUG traces with synthetic phase anomalies. cc @alon.

lucas: thanks team. will upload full traces and sample outputs to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-3142. adding short sample output showing mode: repeat at the end: "...the quick brown fox jumps the and and and"

maya: nice repro. ping when PR lands. :thumbsup:
